input.quote: If a third party claims or threatens a claim that Materials or Base Components IBM provides to Customer or uses in connection with the performance of the Services infringe that party's patent, trademark, copyright, or trade secret, then IBM will indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Customer, its Enterprise and their respective employees, officers, agents and directors against that claim or threatened claim at IBM's expense and pay all costs, damages, penalties and reasonable attorneys' fees that a court finally awards in connection with that claim
input.rationale: Section 8.1 gives us a Vendor-side IP infringement defence and indemnity covering Materials and Base Components, extended to our Enterprise and personnel, with the standard procedure (prompt notice, IBM control, our cooperation — with IBM reimbursing our cooperation costs) and the usual exclusions (our contributed content, our modifications, combinations with non-IBM products, non-IBM hardware/software/data) and remedies (enable continued use, modify, replace, or credit up to 12 months of charges). That is squarely the playbook fallback position, and Section 9.1(a) carves indemnification payments out of IBM's liability cap, so the indemnity is not squeezed by the general cap — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. Noted but not flagged: 8.1 does not add the preferred non-IP heads (breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the infringement remedy is IBM's "entire obligation", and our indemnity in 8.2 is broader than the preferred Customer-content-only scope (notably 8.2(a)(3) for Services Recipient claims, though partly offset by the carve-back in paragraph c for IBM's misconduct or breach). These are sub-elements/other-rule points, not a failure of this rule's fallback, so no redline here.
